werk/nick-lowe-labour-of-lust.text:
Labour of Lust was released in 1979 on Radar Records in England and on Columbia in the United States. Nick Lowe produced it himself. The album was recorded and released at the same time as Dave Edmunds's Repeat When Necessary and has the same Rockpile line-up: Edmunds and Billy Bremner on guitar and Terry Williams on drums. The opener Cruel to Be Kind became Lowe's only big hit in America.

The American release had a different track list. Endless Grey Ribbon was dropped and American Squirm, the British single, was added. On that song Elvis Costello and two members of The Attractions sing and play. Barney Bubbles, who also worked for Costello and Ian Dury, designed the sleeve. The New York Times called it one of the most exuberant and carefully made rock albums of 1979, and The Globe and Mail compared Lowe's feel for arrangements to that of Phil Spector.
werk/nick-lowe-labour-of-lust.listen: Listen to Cruel to Be Kind, the song that opens the album, and notice how short and direct a pop song can be.

werk/nick-lowe-nick-the-knife.text:
Nick the Knife from 1982 is Nick Lowe's third solo album and his first since the break-up of his band Rockpile in 1981. There are still ties to that group: Billy Bremner and Terry Williams play on it, and Heart is a slower version of a Rockpile song that Bremner sang on Seconds of Pleasure.

It is one of only two solo albums without covers: everything was written or co-written by him. Joyce Millman of The Boston Phoenix found him unusually gloomy, on the first album without his old friend Dave Edmunds. He no longer sings his love songs from the safety of the group. The album reached number 50 on the Billboard 200 and number 99 in Britain. In Canada, Stick It Where the Sun Don't Shine made the top 40.
werk/nick-lowe-nick-the-knife.listen: Listen to Heart and note how this song sounds slower than the Rockpile original. Notice what that does to the mood.

werk/nico-chelsea-girl.text:
Chelsea Girl is Nico's first solo album. It was released in October 1967 on Verve Records, produced by Tom Wilson. It followed her work with the Velvet Underground, and the title refers to Andy Warhol's film Chelsea Girls, in which she appeared. At that time she was singing as a folk singer in a coffee house in New York, accompanied by guitarists such as Jackson Browne and by members of the Velvet Underground.

Many songs came from those accompanists: Browne wrote three songs, Lou Reed, John Cale and Sterling Morrison supplied more, and Bob Dylan gave her I'll Keep It with Mine. The accompaniment is sparse, with guitars or keyboards and without drums or bass. Wilson had strings and flute added on top, against the wishes of Nico, who later could no longer listen to the album. On release it made little impression, but later generations became fascinated by its sombre beauty.
werk/nico-chelsea-girl.listen: Listen to I'll Keep It with Mine and notice how thin the accompaniment is around her voice. Can you also hear the strings and the flute that the producer added later?

werk/nico-the-marble-index.text:
The Marble Index is the second album by the German singer Nico, released in November 1968 by Elektra Records. After the folk pop debut Chelsea Girl, she wanted to be taken seriously as an artist and no longer be seen as a former model. Jac Holzman gave her a budget of 10,000 dollars and four days of recording time in Los Angeles. Frazier Mohawk was the producer, but John Cale was given a free hand. He built his arrangements, inspired by modern European classical music, around her harmonium and her sombre voice. The title comes from The Prelude by William Wordsworth.

The album barely registered on release, but gained much appreciation over the years. It sounds bare and cold, and is regarded as a forerunner of the gothic rock of the 1980s.
werk/nico-the-marble-index.listen: In Ari's Song, dedicated to her little son, listen to the harmonium and the vocals: how comforting does this lullaby sound?

werk/nightwish-angels-fall-first.text:
Tuomas Holopainen wrote the music for this album during his military service in the Finnish army. The idea for a band came in August 1996 around a campfire at his summer cottage. Acoustic soon proved too dull, and the group chose a heavier direction. Angels Fall First was actually intended as a demo for record labels, but Spinefarm thought it was perfect and released it unchanged. On 30 September 1997 a limited edition of five hundred copies was released, and on 1 November the regular release followed with four extra tracks.

It is power metal with gothic, folk and classical elements. Tarja Turunen sings, and Holopainen himself sings the male parts on Beauty and the Beast, The Carpenter and Astral Romance. After that he never sang on an album again, because he did not think he was good enough. He now sees the record more or less as an extended demo.
werk/nightwish-angels-fall-first.listen: Listen to Beauty and the Beast and notice the interplay between the female voice of Tarja Turunen and the male voice of Tuomas Holopainen.

werk/nightwish-century-child.text:
Century Child was released in 2002 and is the fourth album by the Finnish band Nightwish. It was the first album with bassist and singer Marko Hietala, who added a male voice to the band alongside the female singer. Also new was the contribution of a real symphony orchestra and a choir. With that the band moved from power metal to a gothic and symphonic sound, with more of a film soundtrack about it.

Keyboardist and songwriter Tuomas Holopainen said that almost all the lyrics were about childhood and the loss of innocence. According to him it is not a concept album, but the themes ran together by themselves. Bless the Child opens the record, End of All Hope and Dead to the World are personal songs about a difficult period in his life. In Finland the album went double platinum.
werk/nightwish-century-child.listen: Listen to Beauty of the Beast and notice how the male voice and the female voice alternate.

werk/nightwish-oceanborn.text:
After the debut Angels Fall First, which was never intended as a real record, the band wanted to pull out all the stops with Oceanborn. The album was released on 7 December 1998 in Finland on Spinefarm Records, with the rest of the world following in the spring of 1999. It is the first record with bassist Sami Vänskä. According to Tuomas Holopainen they still knew little about recording and tried everything: on Moondance there are twenty tracks of violin. That was done in a Finnish school.

The music became more bombastic and more power metal, with faster tempos, melodic guitar and keyboard and plenty of double bass drum, under the influence of Stratovarius. Tarja Turunen's vocals give the whole a dramatic character. Walking in the Air is a cover from the animated film The Snowman. Tapio Wilska sings harshly on The Pharaoh Sails to Orion and Devil & the Deep Dark Ocean. Together with Therion's Theli it is regarded as a cornerstone of symphonic metal.
werk/nightwish-oceanborn.listen: Listen to Moondance and notice the strings. There are twenty tracks of violin on it, so find out how many layers you can distinguish.

werk/nightwish-wishmaster.text:
Wishmaster is the third studio album by the Finnish symphonic metal band. It was released on 8 May 2000 on Spinefarm. Writing and recording went quickly and without fuss, unlike with Oceanborn. Composer Tuomas Holopainen thought it the most detached and least personal album of the band. It came out a few days early, because the music had leaked onto the internet.

The sound continues the bombastic symphonic power metal of Oceanborn, with more emphasis on atmosphere and melody than on speed and heaviness. The fantasy theme is even clearer. There are calmer songs such as Two for Tragedy and Dead Boy's Poem, and a grand piece such as FantasMic. The Kinslayer is about the victims of the shooting at Columbine High School. The album went to number one in Finland.
werk/nightwish-wishmaster.listen: Listen to Dead Boy's Poem, one of the slower songs, and notice how atmosphere and melody take the place of speed.

werk/nils-petter-molv-r-khmer.text:
Khmer by the Norwegian trumpeter, composer and producer Nils Petter Molvær was recorded between 1996 and 1997 and released in 1998 on ECM. The album relies on sampled and artificially created sounds, with house and drum 'n' bass beats underneath. The often slow rhythms are nevertheless played on an acoustic drum kit. He himself plays trumpet, bass and sampler. Others heard include drummer Rune Arnesen and guitarist Eivind Aarset. Manfred Eicher and Ulf Holand produced the record.

The AllMusic reviewer gave it four and a half stars and called it perhaps the most unusual album ECM ever released, because of the then unprecedented mix of jazz and electronics.
werk/nils-petter-molv-r-khmer.listen: In Khmer, listen to how the trumpet blends with samples and acoustic drums.

werk/nils-petter-molv-r-solid-ether.text:
Solid Ether is an album by the Norwegian trumpeter, composer and producer Nils Petter Molvær. He recorded it in 1999, and ECM released it in May of the following year. On the record he plays not only the trumpet but also the piccolo trumpet and the electronic trumpet. He also uses synthesizer, loops, sampler, effects and beats. Guitarist Eivind Aarset, bassist Audun Erlien, drummers Rune Arnesen and Per Lindvall, DJ Strangefruit and singer Sidsel Endresen also play.

The press was enthusiastic. Chris M. Slawecki of All About Jazz spoke of a stunning fusion of classic jazz trumpet styles with techno, drum and bass and electronic music. David R. Adler wrote on AllMusic that not everyone will understand such music, but that it is a seismic shift that has only just begun. Robert Christgau gave it an A and wrote that he dives into chaos and comes out beautifully.
werk/nils-petter-molv-r-solid-ether.listen: Listen to Solid Ether and notice how the trumpet sounds among beats and electronic sounds. What kind of sound does the trumpet make in this environment?

werk/nina-simone-i-put-a-spell-on-you.text:
I Put a Spell on You was recorded in New York in 1964 and 1965 and was released in 1965 on Philips Records. Nina Simone sings and plays piano, and is accompanied by guitarist Rudy Stevenson, among others. Hal Mooney and Horace Ott wrote the arrangements and conducted. The album reached number 99 on the Billboard 200 and number 18 in the British album chart. The title song reached number 28 in the British singles chart.

Critics call it one of her most pop-oriented records, but also one of her best and most consistent. In doing so, according to the review, she gives a sharp edge to songs that might otherwise have sounded saccharine. On the album, Blues on Purpose is a purely jazz instrumental. In 2017, NPR placed the album at number three on a list of the one hundred and fifty greatest albums by women. In 2024, Apple Music put it at number 88 of the best albums of all time.
werk/nina-simone-i-put-a-spell-on-you.listen: Listen to Blues on Purpose, the instrumental on the album. Notice the difference from the songs with vocals: this is jazz without words.

werk/nina-simone-little-girl-blue.text:
Little Girl Blue is Nina Simone's debut. She recorded it in late 1957 in New York for Bethlehem Records, with bassist Jimmy Bond and drummer Tootie Heath. In a thirteen-hour session, fourteen songs were made, of which eleven made the album. She was then in her mid-twenties, still wanted to become a concert pianist and sold the rights straight away for 3,000 dollars. The album lay on the shelf for a long time and was not released until February 1959. In April she signed with Colpix.

Bethlehem then released I Loves You, Porgy as a single, and it became her first hit: number 18 in the pop chart and number 2 in the R&B chart. The album thereby also became a success. In 1987 My Baby Just Cares for Me became a big hit in Britain and Europe, and a reissue followed.
werk/nina-simone-little-girl-blue.listen: In I Loves You, Porgy, listen to how she sings and plays piano with only bass and drums alongside: how little is needed?

werk/nina-simone-nina-simone-sings-ellin.text:
In 1962, Nina Simone recorded songs that Duke Ellington had recorded. He wrote most of them himself or with others, such as Irving Mills and Billy Strayhorn. It was her fourth studio album. She sang, played piano and wrote the arrangements herself. The Malcolm Dodds Singers accompany her.

The sleeve shows only her head, in colour. According to her autobiography, the photograph was meant as an image of her whole body, but she was pregnant with her daughter Lisa at the time. The photographer tried various poses to hide her belly, and probably did not succeed. A leftover shot from the same session she used in 1966 for Nina Simone with Strings.
werk/nina-simone-nina-simone-sings-ellin.listen: In Satin Doll, the only instrumental song, listen to how the piano fares without vocals.

werk/nina-simone-wild-is-the-wind.text:
Wild Is the Wind is Nina Simone's sixth studio album and was released in 1966 on Philips Records. It is not an album that was recorded in one go. It was compiled from recordings that had been left over after the 1964 and 1965 sessions for earlier Philips albums.

The whole is a calm, romantic one built around piano and voice. Black Is the Color of My True Love's Hair was deliberately given little accompaniment: only piano and a bass note. Four Women was released as a single and was banned by the New York jazz station WLIB because of its lyrics. Billboard called the album a special merit pick on release. Later the title song was covered by David Bowie on Station to Station, and Lilac Wine by Jeff Buckley on Grace. In 2020, Rolling Stone placed it at number 212 of the 500 greatest albums ever.
werk/nina-simone-wild-is-the-wind.listen: Listen to Black Is The Color Of My True Love's Hair and notice how little happens around the piano. Can you hear the long, sustained bass note beneath her playing?

werk/nine-inch-nails-ghosts-i-iv.text:
After the tour for Year Zero and his departure from Interscope, Trent Reznor began an experiment in 2007: ten weeks, no fixed plan, everything on impulse. Together with Atticus Ross and Alan Moulder he improvised, helped by Alessandro Cortini, Adrian Belew and drummer Brian Viglione, among others, who built a drum kit out of a rubbish bin, water jugs and a frying pan. It began as an EP of five tracks and became four EPs with thirty-six pieces in all, untitled and almost without vocals. Reznor called it a soundtrack for daydreams.

The album was released in 2008 almost without announcement on Nine Inch Nails' own website, in varying packages and prices. The first nine pieces were free. It was released under a Creative Commons licence. Critics compared the atmosphere to Brian Eno and Robert Fripp. The album was praised for its spirit of experiment and its unusual release and was nominated for a Grammy.
werk/nine-inch-nails-ghosts-i-iv.listen: Listen to track 19, Ghosts III, on which Viglione plays his home-built percussion. Try to hear which sounds seem to come from everyday objects.

werk/nine-inch-nails-pretty-hate-machine.text:
Pretty Hate Machine is the debut album of Nine Inch Nails and was released on 20 October 1989 on TVT Records. Trent Reznor worked at night as a handyman and technician at Right Track Studio in Cleveland. There, in the quiet of the studio, he recorded his own demo, almost entirely by himself. The demo won him a contract with TVT. He recorded the album in various studios with producers he admired, including Flood, Keith LeBlanc and John Fryer. There was no ordinary band.

The sound revolves around synthesizers and drum machines, with catchy riffs and a regular song structure, unlike much other industrial music. The lyrics are about youthful anxiety and the feeling of being betrayed by lovers, society or God. Head Like a Hole is the most rock-like song. The record received very good reviews and became a breakthrough for independently released music, even though Reznor quarrelled with TVT over promotion.
werk/nine-inch-nails-pretty-hate-machine.listen: Listen to Head Like a Hole and notice how the electronic rhythms are combined with guitar.

werk/nine-inch-nails-quake.text:
Quake is the soundtrack of the id Software computer game of the same name from 1996. Trent Reznor made the music with his band Nine Inch Nails and also supplied the sound effects, entirely free of charge, out of mutual admiration for each other's work. The music was on the same disc as the game. Only in 2020 did a vinyl version appear, which also made the official titles known.

It is mostly ambient, and for Reznor it was the first time he had worked with that genre. He himself said that it is not music but textures, atmospheres and turning machine noises, meant to be as sinister as possible. The atmosphere is dark and oppressive, fitting the game. The reactions were positive. GameSpot called it the best soundtrack ever made for a computer game.
werk/nine-inch-nails-quake.listen: Listen to Quake Theme with headphones and notice the dark textures and machine noises. What kind of atmosphere do they evoke in you?

werk/nine-inch-nails-the-downward-spiral.text:
Trent Reznor wrote this concept album after a tour on Lollapalooza, when he felt alienated and was struggling with depression and addiction. He had a quarrel with TVT Records and founded Nothing Records with his manager. The record was mainly recorded in a house in Los Angeles where the Manson Family murders took place in 1969. Reznor turned it into the studio Le Pig. With producer Flood, guitarist Adrian Belew and drummers Chris Vrenna and Stephen Perkins, a sound full of texture came about.

It is industrial rock with techno, metal and ambient, without the usual verse and chorus. Reznor processed guitars and vocals on the computer into abstract sounds. The story follows a man who descends into madness and suicide. The album entered at number two in America and became a cultural phenomenon. It also caused an outcry over crude lyrics, as in Big Man with a Gun.
werk/nine-inch-nails-the-downward-spiral.listen: Listen to Hurt, the closing track: notice how the raw sounds of the rest of the record give way here to something quieter.

werk/nine-inch-nails-the-fragile.text:
After the tour for The Yes Album, the line-up of Yes changed. Keyboardist Tony Kaye did not want to extend his sound beyond organ and piano and had to leave. His successor Rick Wakeman, classically trained, brought Mellotron and Moog and enlarged the band's sonic palette. The recording took place at Advision Studios in London. Because time and money were limited, the album was given a two-part structure: four songs are group pieces, the other five are solo portraits of the band members.

Roundabout and Heart of the Sunrise are the big group pieces. According to Wakeman, the arrangements of both were already fixed after his first day. Roundabout was released in shortened form as a single and brought the group onto American radio. The album also marked the beginning of the long collaboration with the artist Roger Dean, who designed the sleeve. Fragile received glowing reviews and was regarded as the band's breakthrough, and later as a pillar of progressive rock.
werk/nine-inch-nails-the-fragile.listen: Listen to Roundabout and notice the acoustic guitar intro and how the song then grows into a piece with many changes of tempo and mood.

werk/nine-inch-nails-with-teeth.text:
After The Fragile from 1999, Trent Reznor sank into a deep pit: addiction to alcohol and drugs, depression and writer's block. He went to a rehab clinic in Florida and afterwards found that writing came naturally again. He had first conceived a concept record, with a dream from which you cannot wake as an image for getting sober. It became a tight record with the working title Bleedthrough. He dropped that title in October 2004.

With Teeth was released on 3 May 2005 on Nothing Records and Interscope. Reznor produced it with Alan Moulder, and Dave Grohl and Atticus Ross contributed. It is the fourth album by Nine Inch Nails and had three singles: The Hand That Feeds, Only and Every Day Is Exactly the Same. The reviews were good, although somewhat less glowing than for earlier work. Some praised the aggression, others found it colourless.
werk/nine-inch-nails-with-teeth.listen: Listen to The Hand That Feeds and notice how bare and tight the song is built. What is left when there are no extra layers?

werk/nirvana-in-utero.text:
After the polished Nevermind, the band wanted a rawer sound and therefore chose Steve Albini as engineer. In February 1993 they worked for two weeks at Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, Minnesota, in a remote house in the snow. The sessions went quickly. Albini placed about thirty microphones around the drums, and recorded some parts in a kitchen for the natural reverb. Kurt Cobain called it the easiest recording ever.

Afterwards disagreement arose: people at the label found the sound unusable, and the band had doubts about the bass and the vocals. Albini refused to remix. Bob Ludwig mastered the record, and Scott Litt remixed the singles All Apologies, Heart-Shaped Box and Pennyroyal Tea. In Utero topped the American and British charts. Critics praised the lyrics and the raw, idiosyncratic sound. It was the last studio album before Cobain's death.
werk/nirvana-in-utero.listen: Listen to Heart-Shaped Box and notice the difference between the restrained verses and the raw, loud chorus.

werk/nirvana-nevermind.text:
In 1990, Nirvana was already recording songs with producer Butch Vig in Madison, Wisconsin, intended for the label Sub Pop. Then drummer Chad Channing left and Dave Grohl joined. The band signed with DGC Records and insisted on Vig as producer. In May and June 1991 they recorded Nevermind at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys, California, with a budget of 65,000 dollars. It sounded more polished and more radio-friendly than earlier work.

Kurt Cobain wrote most of the songs. The lyrics are about alienation, frustration, anti-establishment ideas, feminist views and relationship problems. Musically the album mixes grunge and alternative rock with acoustic ballads and hard rock with punk influences. Smells Like Teen Spirit was the first single, followed by Come as You Are, Lithium and In Bloom. The album was an unexpected success and brought grunge and alternative rock to a large audience. Critics chose it as the best album of the year in the Pazz & Jop poll.
werk/nirvana-nevermind.listen: In Smells Like Teen Spirit, listen to the contrast between the quiet verses and the loud chorus. Notice how the band creates that difference in volume.

werk/normaal-oerend-hard.text: In 1977, Normaal from the Achterhoek had a hit with Oerend hard, about two drunk motorcyclists and an accident, sung in the Achterhoek dialect. It was probably the first hit in a regional language. The band around singer Bennie Jolink had been founded in 1974 and played raw farmers' rock, in clogs and overalls. Dialect was the language of an identity of its own, of a region that would not be represented by Amsterdam or Hilversum.
werk/normaal-oerend-hard.listen: Put Oerend hard next to Radar Love: two rock songs about the road that nobody would ever confuse with one another.

werk/oasis-be-here-now.text:
After the worldwide successes of Definitely Maybe and (What's the Story) Morning Glory?, everyone was waiting for the third Oasis album. Noel Gallagher wrote most of the songs during a stay on the island of Mustique. The recording took place in various London studios, including Abbey Road, and at Ridge Farm Studio in Surrey. According to co-producer Owen Morris there was a lot of bickering and the band members took drugs. The management restricted the media's access to the album, which turned the press against the band.

The songs are longer than before and contain many guitar overdubs, because Noel wanted the record to sound as colossal as possible. The album became the fastest-selling in British chart history, with D'You Know What I Mean? and All Around the World as number-one singles. First reviews were positive, but later critics called the record bloated and overproduced. Some journalists see its release as the end of Britpop.
werk/oasis-be-here-now.listen: In D'You Know What I Mean?, listen to the thick layer of guitars: try to hear how many parts sound over one another at the same time.

werk/oasis-definitely-maybe.text:
Definitely Maybe is the debut album of Oasis, released in 1994 by Creation Records. The recording began in January at Monnow Valley Studio with producer Dave Batchelor, but it sounded thin and too clean. Only Slide Away survived from those sessions. Batchelor was sacked and the band re-recorded everything at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall, where Noel Gallagher produced himself and added many guitars. That too remained unsatisfactory. Then the manager brought in Owen Morris, who mixed the album and compressed the guitars heavily.

The result sounds raw and full of attacking guitars. Noel wrote all the songs, including Supersonic, Live Forever and Rock 'n' Roll Star. In the United Kingdom the album went straight to number one and was at the time the fastest-selling debut ever. Critics praised the optimistic tone, a counterweight to the gloom of grunge. It is regarded as a cornerstone of Britpop.
werk/oasis-definitely-maybe.listen: In Live Forever, listen to the mood of the song. Notice how hopeful it sounds compared with the dark rock of that time.

werk/oasis-don-t-believe-the-truth.text:
Don't Believe the Truth, Oasis's sixth album, was released on 30 May 2005. The recording dragged on. In January 2004 a first session began at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall with Death in Vegas as producer, but the band was not satisfied with the result. Four songs from that session made the record after all, after extra work or new recordings. After a short break, the band recorded at their own Wheeler End Studios, with Noel Gallagher as producer and The Who's drummer Zak Starkey joining.

For the first time the work was divided among all the band members. Liam Gallagher wrote The Meaning of Soul, Gem Archer A Bell Will Ring. Lyla made it onto the record as the opening single, because the label heard no suitable first single. Critics were positive and called it the band's best record since (What's the Story) Morning Glory?. The album went straight to number one in Britain.
werk/oasis-don-t-believe-the-truth.listen: Listen to A Bell Will Ring, written by guitarist Gem Archer, and notice how a song by a band member other than Noel Gallagher fits into the record.

werk/oasis-heathen-chemistry.text:
Heathen Chemistry, Oasis's fifth album, was released on 1 July 2002. The band recorded it between 2001 and early 2002 at Wheeler End Studios and Olympic Studios in London. It was the first record with guitarist Gem Archer and bassist Andy Bell, and the last with drummer Alan White. For the first time, people other than Noel Gallagher contributed seriously to the writing: Liam Gallagher supplied three songs, Bell and Archer one each.

The sound is simpler than on the psychedelic Standing on the Shoulder of Giants and less heavy than on Be Here Now, and is closer to the first two albums. The Hindu Times became a British number one. Stop Crying Your Heart Out, Little By Little/She Is Love and Songbird, Liam's first song as a writer, were also singles. The reviews were mixed. The album went straight to number one in Britain.
werk/oasis-heathen-chemistry.listen: Listen to The Hindu Times and notice how straightforwardly the band rocks here.

werk/oasis-standing-on-the-shoulder-of-g.text:
After the tour for Be Here Now, the band took a long break for the first time. Noel Gallagher gave up cocaine and wanted a drug-free studio. That led to tension, and during the recording in France, Bonehead and Guigsy left. Their parts were afterwards re-recorded, because Noel played almost all the instruments himself. Producer Owen Morris made way for Mark Stent, and the album was released on the new label Big Brother Recordings. The title is a misquoted remark by Isaac Newton that Noel read on a two-pound coin.

The sound shifts from Britpop to psychedelia with drum loops, samples, electric sitar, Mellotron and reversed guitars. Gas Panic! has trip hop sounds, and with Little James, Liam Gallagher co-wrote a song for the first time.
werk/oasis-standing-on-the-shoulder-of-g.listen: In Gas Panic!, listen to the dark, slow atmosphere and try to pick out the harmonica and the flute.

werk/oasis-what-s-the-story-morning-glor.text:
After Definitely Maybe, Oasis recorded the second album in 1995 in Wales, including at Rockfield Studios. Producers were Owen Morris and guitarist and songwriter Noel Gallagher. Drummer Alan White had just replaced Tony McCarroll. According to Morris the recording was finished in about fifteen days, one song a day. Paul Weller played on Champagne Supernova.

The sound is more spacious than on the debut: more ballads, big choruses and strings, as in Don't Look Back in Anger. Wonderwall is one of the four big hits in England. The prelude was the Battle of Britpop, the chart fight between Roll with It and Blur with Country House. The first reviews were lukewarm, but the verdict turned completely around in the months and years that followed. The record is now regarded as a milestone of Britpop and of the 1990s.
werk/oasis-what-s-the-story-morning-glor.listen: Listen to Don't Look Back in Anger. Notice how the piano opens the song and how the chorus gets all the space, with a guitar solo you can simply sing along to.

werk/olivia-rodrigo-sour.text:
Olivia Rodrigo signed with Geffen Records in 2020 and wanted to release an EP in 2021. Producer Dan Nigro had heard her songs and offered via Instagram to work with her. Because of the pandemic they had a lot of time in the studio. When the debut single drivers license became so big, she decided to turn it into a full album. Rodrigo wrote all the songs together with Nigro, about teenage love, anger, jealousy and sadness.

The album jumps from energetic guitar rock in the style of the 1990s to soft piano ballads and fingerpicked guitars. Rodrigo named Alanis Morissette, Taylor Swift and the White Stripes as inspiration. Songs such as brutal and good 4 u have a danceable, uptempo arrangement, even though they are about unpleasant feelings. Critics praised it as a strong debut with realistic lyrics. It won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album and in 2023 stands at number 358 on Rolling Stone's list.
werk/olivia-rodrigo-sour.listen: In brutal, listen to the energetic guitars, which sound like 1990s rock. Notice how the upbeat tempo clashes with the frustrated lyrics.

werk/oneohtrix-point-never-betrayed-in-t.text:
Betrayed in the Octagon is the first album that Daniel Lopatin released under the name Oneohtrix Point Never, initially as Magic Oneohtrix Point Never. It was released in 2007 on hand-numbered cassettes on the label Deception Island. Two years later a vinyl edition followed on No Fun Records, in which the opening track was dropped and a title was changed.

Lopatin recorded the album in Massachusetts with a Roland Juno-60, a Sequential Circuits Six-Trak and a Roland MSQ-700 sequencer. A reviewer at AllMusic described it as a succession of ghostly elegance and mild new age contemplation. Tracks from the album were reissued in 2009 on the compilation Rifts. The album marks the beginning of the Oneohtrix Point Never project.
werk/oneohtrix-point-never-betrayed-in-t.listen: Listen to Parallel Minds and notice how a small group of synthesizer sounds slowly repeats and shifts. You can hear that the music comes from just a few devices.

werk/oneohtrix-point-never-r-plus-seven.text:
R Plus Seven was released on 30 September 2013 and was Oneohtrix Point Never's first album on Warp Records. Daniel Lopatin worked differently from his previous record Replica, on which he processed old advertising fragments: now he used mainly the synthetic sounds of MIDI instruments, presets from the 1980s and virtual instruments. For the first time his trusty Roland Juno-60 was not heard on it. Lopatin called it a calm album, influenced by his domestic happiness. The title refers to the N+7 method of the writers' group Oulipo.

The record plays with the sounds of old samplers and with church organs and choirs from Hollywood, and sounds, according to Pitchfork, strange and yet full of feeling. Critics compared the rhythms and repetition to Philip Glass and Steve Reich. The reviews were glowing, and the album appeared on various year-end lists. Visual works by artists such as Jon Rafman and Takeshi Murata were also released.
werk/oneohtrix-point-never-r-plus-seven.listen: Listen to Boring Angel and notice the artificial, synthetic sounds that create an atmosphere of their own, a strange one.

werk/oneohtrix-point-never-returnal.text:
Returnal is the fourth studio album by Daniel Lopatin under the name Oneohtrix Point Never, released on 22 June 2010 by Editions Mego. He recorded it with Goldwave and Multiquence, mainly in an air-conditioned room in his parents' house in Massachusetts, in July and August 2009. The first track originated in Brooklyn. Lopatin called it a Rousseau record: a world music record, but hyperreal, seen by someone who is not really in touch with the world.

It builds on his synthesizer music and adds noise and his own processed voice. Nil Admirari opens with noise, rhythm machines and screaming vocals, Describing Bodies and Stress Waves sound almost like hymns. Simon Reynolds described the closing track Preyouandi as an alien landscape of glassy percussion. The reviews were positive and Fact, The Wire and Tiny Mix Tapes named the album one of the best of 2010.
werk/oneohtrix-point-never-returnal.listen: Listen to the closing track Preyouandi and notice the glassy percussion that returns in waves through echo and delay.

werk/oneohtrix-point-never-zones-without.text:
Zones Without People is the second studio album by Daniel Lopatin, who makes electronic music as Oneohtrix Point Never. It was released on 6 August 2009 on Arbor as a limited-edition LP. Most of the material was also on the 2009 compilation Rifts. It is an ambient album that, according to Lopatin, combines several approaches to psychedelic music.

Dreamy synthesizers with reverb build walls of sound. Format & Journey North lasts nine minutes and uses drones, pan flute and water recordings. Pitchfork found the title track beautiful but inhuman. AllMusic and Sputnikmusic gave four out of five, and according to AllMusic the album helped establish Lopatin's name for underwater synthesizers. Stereogum placed it in 2017 eighth out of nine in his discography.
werk/oneohtrix-point-never-zones-without.listen: Listen to Format & Journey North and notice the pan flute and the water recordings between the drones.

werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-a.text:
Architecture & Morality was released on 6 November 1981 and was the third studio album by Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark. The group was looking for a new direction and found it in the emotional power of religious music. Singer Andy McCluskey stressed that he had not become religious, but wanted to understand why people need religion. The band recorded for two months at The Manor Studio and also worked in their own Gramophone Suite in Liverpool. Peter Saville designed the sleeve.

The sound became warmer and more natural, with choir samples and the Mellotron alongside the synthesizers. On the opener The New Stone Age, strikingly many guitars can be heard. Many songs avoid the usual verse and chorus and use long instrumental passages, in which synthesizer lines take the place of the chorus. Souvenir and Joan of Arc became hits. The first reviews were lukewarm, but later the record was regarded as an important synth-pop album.
werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-a.listen: Listen to Souvenir and notice how the choir-like sounds and the synthesizer line together take the place of an ordinary chorus.

werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-d.text:
After the successful Architecture & Morality from 1981, Paul Humphreys and Andy McCluskey had actually wanted to disband OMD. Virgin Records, which had taken over the contract, wanted a copy of that record, but that drove the group in a different direction. They worked in their own Gramophone Suite in Liverpool, with the E-mu Emulator, and later with producer Rhett Davies in Chertsey. The album was released on 4 March 1983.

The record is experimental: sound collages in the style of musique concrète and recordings of shortwave radio about the Cold War and the Eastern Bloc. Radio Prague contains the interval signal of Czechoslovak radio. Time Zones is a montage of speaking clocks from all over the world. Genetic Engineering and Telegraph became singles. The reviews were at first largely negative and the record was regarded as a commercial flop, even though it reached the British top five. Later it grew into a cult classic, praised as an album that was ahead of its time.
werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-d.listen: Listen to Time Zones and notice how speaking clocks from all over the world together form a song.

werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-o.text:
The debut album of the English electronic band Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark was released on 22 February 1980 on Dindisc. Andy McCluskey and Paul Humphreys used the label's advance to build their own studio in Liverpool, The Gramophone Suite, and recorded the album there in three weeks. The songs had been written over four years, Electricity first of all. Kraftwerk, Neu! and Brian Eno were important influences. Many songs revolve around wartime themes.

Electricity and Red Frame/White Light were released as singles, and a new version of Messages became the first hit in the United Kingdom, at number 13. The album reached number 27 and received favourable reviews. The sleeve, designed by Peter Saville and Ben Kelly, had a die-cut grid. The group was dissatisfied with the production, but McCluskey now finds the record full of naivety and energy.
werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-o.listen: Listen to Electricity, the first song the two ever wrote, and notice how minimal the synthesizer lines are.

werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-o.text:
Organisation was released on 24 October 1980 on Dindisc and was the second album by the English band Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark. For the first time the group worked with a producer, Mike Howlett, the former bassist of Gong. Malcolm Holmes became the regular drummer. Most of the songs came about in June and July 1980. The basic tracks were recorded in their own studio in Liverpool, the vocals and extra instruments at Ridge Farm in Rusper.

The tone is darker and more melancholy than on other records by the group. During the writing, Ian Curtis of Joy Division died, and Statues is partly inspired by him. Enola Gay was the only single and reached number 8. The album reached number 6, their first top-10 album in the United Kingdom, and received favourable reviews.
werk/orchestral-manoeuvres-in-the-dark-o.listen: Listen to the beginning of Stanlow: the rhythm opens with the sound of a diesel pump from the refinery where Andy McCluskey's father worked.

werk/ornette-coleman-change-of-the-centu.text:
Change of the Century was released in May 1960 on Atlantic Records. The recording took place on 8 and 9 October 1959 in New York. The group consisted of Ornette Coleman on alto saxophone, Don Cherry on pocket trumpet, Charlie Haden on bass and Billy Higgins on drums. On the sleeve the bandleader wrote that the record was the work of the whole group: beforehand nobody knows what the end result will be, and each player contributes what he feels at that moment.

That approach resonates in the music. The writer A. B. Spellman called the group disciplined, with an enormous mutual intuition. AllMusic wrote that the quartet grew ever more self-assured in its revolutionary approach. The record sold well shortly after its release.
werk/ornette-coleman-change-of-the-centu.listen: In Free, listen to how the saxophone and the pocket trumpet follow and complement each other. Notice how bass and drums move along.

werk/ornette-coleman-ornette-on-tenor.text:
Ornette on Tenor was released in 1962 on Atlantic Records and was the sixth and last album by Ornette Coleman for that label. Here he plays tenor saxophone instead of his usual alto saxophone. Bassist Jimmy Garrison plays, before he joined John Coltrane's quartet. The recording took place on 22 and 27 March 1961 at Atlantic Studios in New York.

It was the last record of the quartet that he had formed in the late 1950s. Later that year he continued with a trio. According to Harvey Pekar of Down Beat, most of the record consists of improvisation, with a few striking compositions. AllMusic found it his least spectacular record for Atlantic, but still far ahead of its time.
werk/ornette-coleman-ornette-on-tenor.listen: In Cross Breeding, listen to the difference in sound between the tenor saxophone and Don Cherry's pocket trumpet.

werk/ornette-coleman-the-shape-of-jazz-t.text:
Ornette Coleman recorded this album on 22 May 1959 at Radio Recorders in Hollywood, after years of odd jobs and a sound that often met with hostility. It was his debut for Atlantic and his first record with the quartet with Don Cherry, Charlie Haden and Billy Higgins. Producer Nesuhi Ertegun came up with the title. Pianist John Lewis had arranged a contract for the saxophonist.

The quartet plays without piano or guitar, so without a chordal instrument. Each piece has a short theme, then a number of minutes of free improvisation, and then the theme returns. The improvisation revolves around melody, not chords. Lonely Woman is one of the few compositions by the saxophonist that became a standard. Shortly after its release, the quartet began a long run of performances at the Five Spot Café in Manhattan, which provoked much discussion. The album helped launch free jazz and was added to the National Recording Registry.
werk/ornette-coleman-the-shape-of-jazz-t.listen: In Lonely Woman, listen to the slow bass, the fast drums and the sad theme that saxophone and cornet play together, bending the notes and making them wail.

werk/oscar-peterson-an-evening-with-osca.text:
An Evening with Oscar Peterson was released in 1952 on Clef Records. The Canadian pianist plays here in a trio with guitarist Barney Kessel and bassist Ray Brown. The twelve tracks include well-known standards, such as Caravan by Duke Ellington and Juan Tizol, I Get a Kick Out of You by Cole Porter, The Way You Look Tonight by Dorothy Fields and Jerome Kern, How High the Moon and The Nearness of You.

In addition there are original pieces, such as Salute to Garner, What Is It?, Minor Blues and Slow Down. Together with the standards they form a programme of short tracks of about three minutes.
werk/oscar-peterson-an-evening-with-osca.listen: Listen to Caravan and notice how, in a trio, piano, guitar and bass each have their own place.

werk/otis-redding-king-en-queen.text:
Producer Jim Stewart came up with this duet album. He thought that the roughness of Otis Redding and the refinement of Carla Thomas would go well together. He also looked at Marvin Gaye, who had had success with his duets. Redding agreed: Thomas, after all, also came from Memphis. They recorded the record in January 1967, while Thomas was studying for a master's degree in English at Howard University.

The work went quickly, in six days or perhaps only three. Booker T. & the M.G.'s, Isaac Hayes and the Memphis Horns played. Ten songs are covers of soul classics; Ooh Carla, Ooh Otis was written by Redding together with Al Bell. Tramp and Knock On Wood became hits. King & Queen became Redding's last studio album before his death in December 1967. Later reviewers praised the chemistry between the two singers and the light, humorous character of the record.
werk/otis-redding-king-en-queen.listen: Listen to Tramp and notice how the two voices tease each other: Redding's rough voice against Thomas's smoother one.

werk/otis-redding-otis-blue-otis-redding.text:
Otis Redding had been signed by Stax Records in 1962 after the label heard him sing at an audition. His third album was released in 1965 on Volt, a subsidiary of Stax. On 9 and 10 July he recorded it, with one exception in less than twenty-four hours, at the Stax studio in Memphis, with the house band Booker T. & the M.G.'s, a horn section and Isaac Hayes on piano.

Most of the material consists of covers, including three songs by Sam Cooke, who had been shot dead a few months earlier, and three original songs. So you hear the singer in Respect, in A Change Is Gonna Come and in the Rolling Stones' Satisfaction, which he plays in his own way. Ole Man Trouble opens the record, and he co-wrote I've Been Loving You Too Long. Critics see the album as his first fully successful LP and as the benchmark for soul of that time.
werk/otis-redding-otis-blue-otis-redding.listen: In Respect, listen to the energy of the vocals and to the horns driving the song. Notice how the singer asks for respect with full conviction.

werk/otis-redding-pain-in-my-heart.text:
Pain in My Heart is Otis Redding's debut and contains recordings from 1962 and 1963. He recorded for Volt, a subsidiary of Stax in Memphis, and the album was released on 17 March 1964 on Atco. His first single, These Arms of Mine, came from a session in which he was actually just the driver of guitarist Johnny Jenkins. When the session finished early, he was allowed to sing two songs, and Stax signed him.

The title song was written by Allen Toussaint under the name Naomi Neville. It resembled a song by Irma Thomas so closely that copyright issues arose. There are also covers of Stand By Me, Louie Louie, Lucille and The Dog. The critic Rob Bowman heard in the title song how the singer uses his voice like a horn, swelling and growing soft. AllMusic gave four stars.
werk/otis-redding-pain-in-my-heart.listen: Listen to Pain In My Heart and notice how the voice swells and sinks away, and how the word heart is worked over again and again.

werk/otis-redding-the-great-otis-redding.text:
This second album by Otis Redding was released in March 1965 and was his first for the new label Volt, a subsidiary of Stax. It was recorded at the Stax studio in Memphis, with Booker T. & the M.G.'s and the Memphis Horns as accompanists. Engineer Tom Dowd provided a stereo mix. As the title says, most of the twelve songs are soul ballads.

The album opens with That's How Strong My Love Is, which came out days after the original version by O. V. Wright and was covered shortly afterwards by the Rolling Stones. Mr. Pitiful was written by guitarist Steve Cropper together with the singer, in the car on the way to the studio, prompted by the nickname a disc jockey had given him. It became his first single in the top ten. The critical response was mixed: AllMusic gave three stars, the Rolling Stone Album Guide five.
werk/otis-redding-the-great-otis-redding.listen: Listen to Mr. Pitiful and notice how the singer plays with the nickname from which the song began: a man who sounds pitiful when he sings a ballad.

werk/otis-redding-the-soul-album.text:
The Soul Album was released in April 1966 and is Otis Redding's fourth studio album. It came after Otis Blue, whose sleeve had still concealed the singer's origins. Now there was a portrait of an African American woman in a headscarf, in full colour.

The record contains original songs and arrangements of songs by Sam Cooke, Eddie Floyd, Roy Head and Smokey Robinson. Guitarist Steve Cropper played and is credited as co-writer on three songs. Others heard include Booker T. Jones, Isaac Hayes, bassist Donald Dunn and drummer Al Jackson Jr. A reviewer at AllMusic felt that Redding remade the songs so that they were no longer covers but interpretations of his own. He called Cigarettes and Coffee the jewel of an underrated record.
werk/otis-redding-the-soul-album.listen: Listen to Chain Gang and compare it in your mind with Sam Cooke's original: where does Redding make it his own, rougher soul version?

werk/oumou-sangare-ko-sira.text:
Ko Sira is a 1993 album by the Malian Wassoulou singer Oumou Sangaré. It was first released independently under the title Bi Furu. The record was made in Berlin and produced by Nick Gold and Massambou Welle Diallo. She wrote the songs herself, and like much of her work the album deals with feminist themes. The title refers to the marriage of today. Sigi Kuruni is about the possibility of domestic violence in a new marriage.

Critics praised her high, soulful singing above a mixture of Western guitar, bass and violin with African percussion and call-and-response vocals. In Europe the album was a commercial success and stayed for months in the world music charts.
werk/oumou-sangare-ko-sira.listen: In Sigi Kuruni, listen to the high vocals and the two backing singers who answer them.

werk/outkast-aquemini.text:
Aquemini is OutKast's third album, released in 1998 by LaFace and Arista. The title combines the star signs of the two rappers: Big Boi is Aquarius, André 3000 Gemini. That difference in character runs through the record as a theme. After the success of ATLiens, the duo were given more money and freedom. The recording took place mostly in Atlanta, at Bobby Brown's Bosstown Recording Studios and Doppler Studios. They lived in the studio for weeks, produced most of it themselves and let session musicians drift in and out. Many songs grew out of jam sessions.

The sound has live instruments and influences of 1970s funk, southern soul, gospel, country and psychedelic rock. Guests include Raekwon, George Clinton and Erykah Badu. Critics were very enthusiastic about the musicianship and the idiosyncratic themes. The album went platinum in two months and is regarded as one of the best hip hop albums ever.
werk/outkast-aquemini.listen: In the title track Aquemini, listen to the two rappers. Notice how different they sound, because that contrast is the theme of the record.

werk/outkast-atliens.text:
OutKast's second album was released in 1996. The debut Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik had made the group known, but at the 1995 Source Awards the duo were booed. André 3000 answered that the South had something to say. The label gave the two more creative freedom, and they recorded in various studios in Atlanta and New York. They wrote some thirty-five songs and kept fourteen. For the first time they produced themselves, under the name Earthtone III, alongside Organized Noize.

The record sounds spacious and calm, with lots of echo and reverb from dub and reggae, and gospel influences. Elevators (Me & You) was the first song they made together, and Wheelz of Steel stands out for Mr. DJ's scratching. The title combines ATL, Atlanta, with aliens. Critics read in it a feeling of alienation from American society. The record was received with praise.
werk/outkast-atliens.listen: Listen to Elevators (Me & You). Notice the echo, the dub-like bass and the organ, and hear how the elevator in the lyrics is an image for the ups and downs of fame.

werk/outkast-speakerboxxx-the-love-below.text:
This double album consists of two solo records released under the duo's name. After his first Grammy, André 3000 wanted to do something different and tried an acting career in Los Angeles. That went moderately, and he began making an album of his own at home with Pro Tools, a drum machine and synthesizers. Big Boi then decided that his next project would be Speakerboxxx. Arista felt that separate solo albums were not suitable at that moment and bundled them into an album of more than two hours.

Speakerboxxx is Southern hip hop under the influence of Parliament-Funkadelic, with lyrics about single parenthood, religion and politics, among other things. The Love Below largely abandons hip hop for pop, funk, jazz and psychedelia, inspired by Prince, and revolves around love. Hey Ya! and The Way You Move reached the top of the American Hot 100. The album won a Grammy for Album of the Year, only the second hip hop record to manage that.
werk/outkast-speakerboxxx-the-love-below.listen: Listen to Hey Ya! and notice how cheerful the music sounds, while you can follow the lyrics about a love that is not working.

werk/ozzy-osbourne-bark-at-the-moon.text:
Bark at the Moon is Osbourne's third solo album, after he had left Black Sabbath in 1979. It was released in late 1983 and was his first record with guitarist Jake E. Lee. Drummer Tommy Aldridge played only on this album. Bob Daisley was on bass, Don Airey played keyboards, and Max Norman was co-producer and engineer.

The title song was released as the first single, with the first music video the singer ever made. Many fans thought the choice of the ballad So Tired as second single was pointless. A quarrel arose over the credits: officially everything was in the singer's name, but Lee and Daisley said that they made a large part of the music and the lyrics. Now You See It (Now You Don't) was, according to Daisley, a dig at Sharon, the singer's manager and wife, who had fired him in 1981. The album was a commercial success and quickly went gold in the United States.
werk/ozzy-osbourne-bark-at-the-moon.listen: Listen to the title song Bark at the Moon and notice how the guitar and the vocals together drive the song forward.

werk/ozzy-osbourne-blizzard-of-ozz.text:
After Black Sabbath had fired him in 1979, because his drug problems caused tension, Ozzy Osbourne signed with Jet Records and set up a solo band. The debut album was released in September 1980 in England and in March 1981 in America. He wrote a large part of it with guitarist Randy Rhoads and bassist Bob Daisley, who stayed temporarily at the Welsh Monnow Valley Studio. Later Lee Kerslake became the regular drummer. It was recorded at Ridge Farm Studio. Because the band was dissatisfied, Max Norman took over the production from Chris Tsangarides.

Crazy Train and Mr. Crowley were released from the album as singles. Goodbye to Romance was the first song to be written and is, according to Osbourne, a farewell to Black Sabbath. Dee is an instrumental piece by Rhoads for his mother. A controversy later arose around Suicide Solution. Even so, the album received much praise and in 2017 stood at number nine on a Rolling Stone list of the best metal albums.
werk/ozzy-osbourne-blizzard-of-ozz.listen: Listen to Dee and notice Randy Rhoads's guitar playing without vocals or band around it. He wrote this piece for his mother.

werk/ozzy-osbourne-diary-of-a-madman.text:
Diary of a Madman was released in October 1981 and is Ozzy Osbourne's second album. It is the last with guitarist Randy Rhoads, who was killed in a plane crash in March 1982 during the tour. The sleeve shows Rudy Sarzo and Tommy Aldridge, but the bass and drums on the original release were played by Bob Daisley and Lee Kerslake. Daisley also wrote part of the music and most of the lyrics. Both were fired shortly after the recording and received no credit, which later led to a lawsuit.

On release the reviews were often lukewarm. Rolling Stone found the songs little more than riffs with a vocal line on top. Later the appreciation grew. Critics above all praise Rhoads's neoclassical guitar work and the mystical, eerie atmosphere. According to AllMusic, some fans prefer this album to Blizzard of Ozz. In 2017 it stood at number 15 on Rolling Stone's list of the best metal albums.
werk/ozzy-osbourne-diary-of-a-madman.listen: Listen to the title song Diary of a Madman and notice how Rhoads's guitar sets the mood. That way you hear why critics praise his playing so highly.

werk/ozzy-osbourne-the-ultimate-sin.text:
After a stay in rehab at the Betty Ford Center, the singer was presented in 1985 with a lot of music by guitarist Jake E. Lee. This time Lee demanded a contract with his writing credits before he delivered anything, because he had been sidelined on the previous album. Bob Daisley wrote the lyrics for the most part, but no longer played. Phil Soussan took over on bass, Randy Castillo came in behind the drums, and Ron Nevison produced. The working title was Killer of Giants, but at the last moment it became The Ultimate Sin.

Shot in the Dark became the hit single. Soussan co-wrote it, and the song was originally by his previous band Wildlife. The album went platinum in 1986 and was his best-charting studio record up to that point. Even so, he calls it his least favourite solo album: he found Nevison's production unimaginative.
werk/ozzy-osbourne-the-ultimate-sin.listen: Listen to Shot in the Dark and notice the balance between guitar and vocals: what stands out most in the chorus?

werk/parliament-chocolate-city.text:
In 1975, Parliament released their third album, as a tribute to Washington, D.C., where the group was particularly popular. The name comes from an expression that black radio stations in the city had used since the early 1970s, because black people were becoming the majority there. George Clinton made a positive image of it in the title song. The sleeve shows the Capitol, the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial in the shape of a chocolate medallion. The classic P-Funk line-up plays on the record, along with guests such as the Brecker Brothers and singer Glenn Goins. There is a lot of fast funk and group singing. Let Me Be draws on jazz and gospel, and I Misjudged You is a tribute to the Unifics from Washington.

In the capital alone, 150,000 copies were sold.
werk/parliament-chocolate-city.listen: Listen to Chocolate City and notice the lyrics, in which Clinton lists cities and calls Washington the capital of all chocolate cities.
